I will compare the pre-play-adjustment severity-weighted player score from weighted_pressure_view with the current side-balance team score. I will restrict to the 34 tightened current candidates, rank player scores within that pool and team scores across the current team view using higher-is-better percentiles, then return the six largest player-minus-team percentile conflicts.

I will assemble the six requested score pictures, restrict to the 34 current candidates before ranking, and compute each candidate’s mean rank and rank variability across pictures. I expect a stable-leader report limited to mean rank in the better half of the pool and separate low-variability/high-variability top-five reports.

I will identify the most rank-sensitive current candidate as the current-pool player with the largest rank range across the six pictures, then decompose his current score relative to the first event-ledger picture. The output will include speed, pressure-quality, and play shifts, latest eligibility, and the current team score versus the median team score.

The first decomposition failed because the supplied scored table does not contain event-pressure percentile or play-adjustment columns. I will repair the inputs using the first classification table for event pressure, the play-adjusted table for the short-window adjustment, and the current category view for the retained current score; the rank-sensitive candidate should be Jawaan Taylor, identified by the largest six-picture rank range.

I will reopen only the seven high-leverage mismatch cases into the 34-player current candidate pool, using unchanged mismatch-aware player scores and play counts. I will recompute the weakest-link score and side-balance adjustment for each comparable team, then compare it with the current team score and rank by absolute movement.

Build a stress-tested view for the current robust-elite members by applying 0.10 times only positive averaged season-strong versus play-weak conflict gap to current scores. I will separately report elites with a positive penalty, count elites without matched example-play evidence, and rank the five unchecked elites by their unpenalized current score.

Repair the stress-test join so all robust elites receive their averaged conflict gap and play-check status; the summary should show the elite total, weakened subset, and unchecked subset, while the two reports should show the requested weakened players and five highest-scoring unchecked elites.
Resolve the column collision by renaming averaged play evidence before the left join; then the stress penalty and unchecked status can be computed from the explicit renamed fields.

The stress view now executes and shows 9 robust elites, 8 unchecked, and no positive penalties; downstream reports still reference the old conflict column name. I will repoint both reports to the repaired names and re-read the summary and top unchecked elites.

I will join the current robust-elite labels, six-picture stability metrics, full heavier-severity sensitivity, and play-conflict stress results on cleaned player identity. I will compute the three candidate-pool 75th-percentile cutoffs (with zero stress drop for unchecked players), retain robust elites meeting every cutoff, and rank missed robust elites by the specified summed burden.

The prior final-consensus process used player_picture_comparison as the category input, which lacks category_labels; I will correct the input wiring and compute all three cutoffs strictly over the 34 current candidates. Stress drops come from the elite stress view, with unmatched/unchecked players assigned measured drop 0 while preserving play_checked.

The stress table contains only robust elites and therefore lacks current_candidate; I will attach eligibility from current_category_view before calculating the current-pool stress cutoff, treating current candidates without a stress check as zero drop as specified. Then the qualified and miss reports will recompute.

I will combine the current side-aware team scores, mixed-middle scores, consensus-player counts, and re-entry fragility for all comparable teams. I expect a five-row final consensus report and a separate ranking of the current top-five leaders by absolute re-entry movement, with larger fragility receiving the larger penalty percentile.

Build the raw-table shortcut on all 86 players, then audit its strongest players who are absent from the final consensus and compare simple shortcut team averages with final team scores. I expect five player audit rows and five teams with the largest positive shortcut overstatement among teams having final scores.

Repair the player shortcut audit to use the final consensus table's team_clean identity while preserving the raw-table shortcut scores. The player audit should now show the five highest shortcut-score players not in the final consensus, alongside their shortcut ranks and component percentiles; the team overstatement table is already valid.

The repaired audit still fails because the raw shortcut retains `team` rather than `team_clean`. Rename that identity inside the callback before joining to the final consensus keys; this should produce the requested five player shortcut audit rows without changing the already verified team audit.

This audit needs one consistent comparison across the saved alternate player and team views. The observed table should contain one row per audited choice with its domain, set distance, added names, and missed final names; I will then rank the five largest distances separately across both domains.
